newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle slip late, close lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle slip late, close lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures slipped late with a lack of fed cattle trade and mostly lower boxed beef values weighing on the market, traders said.
The market grew increasingly disappointed that packers have not raised bids for cattle and mostly lower boxed beef values at noon reinforced the bearish sentiment, traders said.
"Mostly lower beef despite the reduced slaughter shows lack of demand for beef," one trader said.
Live cattle had followed the lead of other livestock pits and moved up to post early gains before drifting back on the lack of cash cattle sales, traders said.
LFG, Refco and Smith Barney sold December late with pressure cited in spot October, traders said. R.J. O'Brien sold October early, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, Dean Witter bought February 70 calls and commission houses bought February 62 puts early. Later trade saw selling of the February 60/70 strangle. Volatility was steady to lower in December, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures traded on both sides of previous levels early before falling late when scattered selling met little resistance and sell stops were touched off. Higher corn futures and slipping prices in live cattle futures as well as a lower CME index weighed on the market late, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.59 at $63.29 per cwt, the lowest level since September 5.

Stone Traders was a notable seller with Lind-Waldock also selling late. ADM Investor Services spread long November/short October. Cargill Investor Services and Shatkin bought January and May early, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.200 cent a lb lower to 0.050 higher with December off most at 66.200 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.500 cent lower to 0.125 higher with October off 0.150 at 63.500.
